title: Existence of the finite etale trace family
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For an object $w:W\to X$ of the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] write $W_Y=W\times_XY$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projection $p_W:W_Y\to W$; $W_Y$ with $w\circ p_W$ is an object of $X_{\Et}$, and with its projection to $Y$ an object of $Y_{\Et}$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. For an abelian sheaf $F$ on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and an etale $j:V\to X$ let $\rho^j_F:j^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}F|_V$ be the isomorphism, natural in $F$, of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction] ($F|_V(V'\to V)=F(V'\to V\to X)$). Since $(f_*f^{-1}F)(W)=(f^{-1}F)(W_Y)$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], $c_{F,W}=\rho^f_F(W_Y):(f_*f^{-1}F)(W)\xrightarrow{\sim}F(W_Y)$. For a morphism $\operatorname{tr}:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$ write $\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_W=\operatorname{tr}(W)\circ c_{F,W}^{-1}:F(W_Y)\to F(W)$.

Then there is a family of morphisms of abelian sheaves $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}:f_*f^{-1}F\to F$, indexed by all finite etale morphisms $f:Y\to X$ (all schemes $X$) and all $F\in\Ab(X_{\Et})$, with the following properties (no uniqueness is asserted here):

(0) *naturality in $F$*: for every morphism $\varphi:F\to G$ in $\Ab(X_{\Et})$, $\varphi\circ\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}=\operatorname{tr}_{f,G}\circ f_*f^{-1}\varphi$;

(1) *compatibility with etale localization on $X$*: let $g:X'\to X$ be etale, $Y'=Y\times_XX'$ and $f':Y'\to X'$ the projection (finite etale [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]). For an object $W\to X'$ of $X'_{\Et}$, regarded as the object $W\to X'\xrightarrow{g}X$ of $X_{\Et}$, let $\kappa_W:W\times_{X'}Y'\xrightarrow{\sim}W\times_XY$ be the canonical isomorphism over $W$ (pasting of cartesian squares [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting]). Then for every such $W$
$$\rho^g_F(W)\circ\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f',g^{-1}F,W}=\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f,F,W}\circ F(\kappa_W)^{-1}\circ\rho^g_F(W\times_{X'}Y'):(g^{-1}F)(W\times_{X'}Y')\to F(W)$$
(this is the componentwise form of $g^{-1}\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}=\operatorname{tr}_{f',g^{-1}F}$ under the canonical identification $g^{-1}f_*f^{-1}F\cong f'_*f'^{-1}g^{-1}F$, both sides of which have $F(W\times_XY)$ as sections over $W$);

(2) *the split case*: suppose $Y=\coprod_{j\in J}V_j$ for a finite set $J$ (possibly empty) and pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $V_j$ covering $Y$, such that each $f|_{V_j}:V_j\to X$ is an isomorphism; let $s_j:X\to Y$ be its inverse followed by the inclusion. For an object $w:W\to X$ of $X_{\Et}$ let $\sigma_{j,W}=(\mathrm{id}_W,s_j\circ w):W\to W_Y$ (a morphism of $X_{\Et}$). Then for every $W$ and every $t\in F(W_Y)$,
$$\overline{\operatorname{tr}}_{f,F,W}(t)=\sum_{j\in J}F(\sigma_{j,W})(t).$$
In particular, for $Y=\coprod_{i=1}^dX$ ($d\ge0$, the coproduct of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-copies]) and $f$ the identity on each summand, take $V_i$ the image of the $i$-th coprojection: under $(f_*f^{-1}F)(W)\cong F(W)^d$, $t\mapsto(F(\sigma_{i,W})c_{F,W}(t))_i$ (an isomorphism by the sheaf condition; this reformulation is not part of the assertion), $\operatorname{tr}_{f,F}$ is the sum map $F^{\oplus d}\to F$.

source.place: Stacks Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE: 'The trace map is characterized by the following two properties ... Hence we can define the trace map using the characterization given'; uses Etale Morphisms Lemma 04HN (etale.tex, lemma-finite-etale-etale-local)

proof.text: For each finite etale morphism choose the natural transformation supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-descent], together with its local sum characterizations. Define the global family by evaluating each chosen natural transformation at the sheaf $F$.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: The naturality identity for the chosen natural transformation, reversed and with the composite functor unfolded, is exactly property (0).

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: For each etale localization, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-localization] to the chosen component for $f,F$ and the chosen component for $f^{\prime},g^{-1}F$. Their local sum characterizations are part of the chosen witnesses. Associativity gives precisely property (1), for every isomorphism with the two specified projection identities.

source.place: Section 03SH (section-trace-method), paragraph after Definition 03SE; descent details as in SGA 4, Expose IX, 5.1.

proof.text: For a global finite clopen splitting, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-trace-pullback-sum] to the chosen component and its local sum characterization. This is property (2) for every site object, including the empty splitting.
